headline: Oilers activate Zach Hyman, Devon Levi off IR
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Oilers have activated Zach Hyman and Devon Levi from injured reserve. Per the outlet, both had been out of the lineup for about two weeks with various injuries.

So far this season, Hyman has one goal in six games, but the chances say that's bad luck more than bad play. He was expected to score about 1.84 goals (expected goals measure the quality of the chances a player takes part in) and has 1.0, a gap of 0.84. At five-on-five, EDM has taken 47.4 percent of the expected goals with him on the ice, and his model rate of 1.39 per 60 minutes is solid. Last season he scored 31 goals in 58 games, so we'd expect the goals to come. For fantasy owners, he's worth holding. Levi is the bigger question. His .886 save percentage in seven games has cost EDM 1.25 goals compared with what an average goalie would allow on those shots (goals saved above expected). The team has the same issue overall, at 3.9 goals below expected in net, even though its 11-3-3 record looks strong. The offense has covered for it, and Levi's play is the thing to watch.
